Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

shot noun

at goal, in a ball game

also a shot at goal, take a shot, shoot (at goal), good shot!

classical

Cic. Div. 2.121: tālōrum jactus (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. throw, shot (Mercuriale 1569: omnem pilae jactum)
Traupman 46

jactus, jactūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a throw, a shot (with the hand)

Any throw or cast, and the throw of dice (Cic. Div. 2.121). In ball games, a thrown shot (M-O; Traupman 46, a free throw jactus ā līneā). A kicked shot is ictus.

Other words

  • ictus, ictūs m. — a blow, a stroke; a kick at the ball

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.19 (Lewis & Short)

    Classically a blow, a stroke or a sting; for a kick at goal, ictus with pede, as one says pilam pede īcere (see kick).

Examples

  • Ingēns profectō jactus.

    What a throw! (at bowls)Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs (ūnus fōns)

See also goal, kick, throw, score, point.
